subject: FinBank VPC connector requirements — follow-up & action log
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Samir Iqbal <samir@finbank.com>, Procurement <procurement@finbank.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T10:15:00-04:00
Subject: FinBank demo + next steps on private connectivity

Hi Samir — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we have a single action log.

Summary from call:
- FinBank primary requirement: keep PII/PHI traffic in a private network; public-hosted endpoints not acceptable for production.
- Short-term: start with a Private VPC (Redwood Private) in AWS (us-east-1) with PrivateLink if possible; long-term: evaluation of on-prem connector.
- Key teams: Network (Alice), Security (procurement CC'd), Platform (you).

Technical asks I need to confirm before we scope a SOW: 
1) Do you prefer AWS PrivateLink (endpoint service) or VPC Peering for initial rollout? We can support both; PrivateLink gives stricter one-way ingress.
2) VPC details: target VPC CIDR and whether you will provision a PrivateLink endpoint in us-east-1.
3) Allowlist needs: will you consume static egress IP ranges or will you configure endpoint policies?
4) Compliance items: Do you need SOC2 evidence and encryption certs (we can attach SOC2 report and KMS integration notes).

Proposed next steps:
- Samir/Alice to confirm preferred connectivity option and provide a network contact (NAT egress IPs or endpoint VPC ID) by EOD Wed (9/1).
- Redwood to share a concise network checklist + sample allowlist and a PrivateLink wiring diagram (attached).
- Schedule a 30-min handoff call between your network team and our infra engineer (Lauren) next week.

Attachments: finbank-demo-notes.pdf (demo highlights)

Thanks — I copied Lauren to own the handoff scheduling and Sergio to advise on dedicated capacity pricing if you decide to reserve GPUs later.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Samir Iqbal <samir@finbank.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@finbank.com>, Alice Network <alice.network@finbank.com>
Date: 2026-08-31T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Re: FinBank demo + next steps on private connectivity

Aditya — thanks for the clear recap. A few quick answers from our side:

- Preference: PrivateLink first. Our security team prefers endpoint-style connectivity to avoid broad route propagation.
- I'll loop in Alice (network lead) who will pull the VPC IDs and shared subnet info.
- On allowlists: we can add Redwood egress IPs to our outbound firewall. We'll need your published list (or a small set of NAT IPs) for the allowlist.
- Compliance: Procurement asked for a SOC2 summary and TLS/kms notes — they are on copy.

I'll aim to get the network contact details and a preliminary decision on region (us-east-1 preferred) by 2026-09-01. If that slips, we'll update you.

Samir
Samir Iqbal
Senior Platform Manager, FinBank
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Samir Iqbal <samir@finbank.com>
Cc: Alice Network <alice.network@finbank.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T08:30:00-04:00
Subject: Re: FinBank demo + next steps on private connectivity

Thanks Samir — great, PrivateLink path makes sense. Attached a short tech checklist and two small artifacts we typically hand to customer network teams. See highlights / asks below.

Redwood connectivity checklist (PrivateLink):
- Customer action: Create a VPC Endpoint (Interface) in target region (us-east-1) and share subnet IDs and security-group used for the endpoint.
- Customer action: Provide the VPC ID and whether there are NACLs that could block outbound TLS (443).
- Redwood action: Provide the list of NAT/egress IPs we will use for callbacks and telemetry (we will publish a stable list during provisioning).
- Optional: If you want mutual TLS between the endpoint and Redwood, indicate and we'll include cert exchange steps in SOW.

Sample allowlist file attached (sample-allowlist.txt) — this includes the example egress IPs we allocate for customers in the us-east-1 hosted fleet; if you select Dedicated we'll provide a narrower set tied to the reserved pool.

Scheduling: Lauren — can you propose two slots next week for a 30-min network handoff? We should include Alice and one of our infra engineers (Sergio).

Next proposed dates for the handoff: 2026-09-07 11:00-11:30 ET or 2026-09-08 15:00-15:30 ET — please confirm.

Attachments: redwood-privatelink-reference.pdf, sample-allowlist.txt

—Aditya
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T16:05:00-04:00
Subject: Internal: Draft SOW and procurement checklist for FinBank (for your review)

Aditya / Sergio — quick internal note after Samir's reply. I'm drafting a short SOW that scopes an initial PrivateLink-only rollout (1 region, 3 availability subnets) with an option to convert to Dedicated later. Items I'm including:
- Network wiring deliverables (endpoint wiring diagram, allowlist file).
- Compliance attachments (SOC2 summary included as exhibit).
- Standard 30-day provisioning SLA for Private customer setup; 60-day for Dedicated.
- Pricing footnote for egress IP reservation if FinBank wants a fixed NAT pool.

I'll share a draft in Drive and ping procurement to start the legal review once Samir confirms network details. Sergio, please add a short block on Dedicated capacity lead time and estimated monthly unit cost so procurement has visibility.

Lauren
Head of Customer Success Operations, Redwood Inference
